**1. INTRODUCTION**

This report presents the annual performance evaluation of Hanson Building Materials Ltd (supplier code HBM-015) for the calendar year 2024. The assessment is based on delivery records, quality inspection reports, site feedback, and commercial correspondence held by the Procurement Department. The purpose of the review is to determine the supplier's continued suitability for the approved vendor list and to identify areas for improvement ahead of the 2025 framework agreement.

The rating scale used throughout this report is 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). A score of 3.0 is considered the minimum acceptable threshold for continued inclusion on the approved supplier list without a corrective action plan. Scores below this threshold trigger a formal performance review meeting.

**2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

Hanson Building Materials Ltd has maintained a strong performance record throughout the 2024 evaluation period. The supplier has consistently met the project delivery schedules for the Northgate Retail Park development and the A12 Junction Improvement Scheme, with only two minor delays recorded, both of which were resolved within 48 hours and did not impact the critical path.

The overall supplier rating for the 2024 review period is **4.2 out of 5.0**, reflecting a solid performance across all assessed categories. This rating is current as of the date of issue of this report and supersedes the interim mid-year score of 3.9 issued in July 2024. The supplier evaluation report for Hanson Building Materials Ltd rates has_supplier_rating 4.2. Record status: current.

Areas of particular strength include material quality consistency, responsiveness to site queries, and adherence to health and safety documentation requirements. The primary area for improvement identified during the period is delivery punctuality on smaller, ad-hoc orders, where performance was marginally below the target level.

**3. SCORING METHODOLOGY**

Each performance category is scored based on a weighted average of monthly assessments submitted by site managers and the procurement team. Monthly assessment forms are completed within five working days of the end of each month, with a consolidated score calculated by the Procurement Contracts Team. The categories and their respective weightings for 2024 are as follows:

| Category | Weighting |
|----------|-----------|
| Delivery Punctuality | 30% |
| Quality of Materials | 35% |
| Commercial Responsiveness | 15% |
| Health & Safety Documentation | 10% |
| Communication & After-Sales Support | 10% |

Individual monthly scores are recorded in the supplier performance database (reference SP-2024-HBM). A summary of the quarterly scores is provided in Section 5 below.

**4. DELIVERY PUNCTUALITY**

Delivery punctuality is assessed against the agreed delivery dates and times specified on purchase orders. For the 2024 period, a total of 214 deliveries were scheduled across all active projects. Of these, 198 were delivered on time or early, representing a punctuality rate of 92.5%. This is slightly below the internal target of 95% but remains within the acceptable range for the rating scale.

The table below presents the consolidated monthly scores by quarter for the 2024 review period. Scores are the weighted average per the methodology in Section 3. All scores are recorded in the supplier performance database (reference SP-2024-HBM).

The Q3 dip in delivery punctuality corresponds to the period when ad-hoc order lead times were extended due to the supplier's internal transport reorganisation. This was raised at the quarterly review meeting on 3 October 2024 and a corrective action plan was agreed. Improvement was observed in Q4.

**6. PERFORMANCE BY CATEGORY – DETAILED COMMENTS**

**6.1 Delivery Punctuality (Annual score: 4.0)**

As noted in Section 4, the annual punctuality rate was 92.5%. The shortfall against the 95% target was concentrated in small orders under £500 and in deliveries to the North Shields site, where access restrictions occasionally required re-timing. The supplier's transport team has proposed a revised delivery window for that site, effective from February 2025.

**6.2 Quality of Materials (Annual score: 4.5)**

Material quality was consistently high throughout the year. No NCRs were raised against Hanson Building Materials Ltd in 2024. One minor issue was noted in June regarding a batch of bagged cement that had hardened due to storage conditions at the supplier's depot; this was replaced within 48 hours at no cost. The site team at the Riverside development reported no repeat occurrences.

**6.3 Commercial Responsiveness (Annual score: 4.1)**

Quotations for variations and new orders were returned within the agreed 5-working-day period in 89% of cases. The remaining 11% were delayed by an average of 2 working days, usually where pricing required confirmation from the supplier's regional office. Pricing remained competitive against the benchmark rates held by the procurement team.

**6.4 Health & Safety Documentation (Annual score: 4.6)**

All safety data sheets, delivery notes, and vehicle documentation were received in good order. The supplier's drivers have consistently complied with site induction requirements. No instances of missing or incomplete documentation were recorded during the period.

**6.5 Communication & After-Sales Support (Annual score: 4.2)**

The named account manager responded to email queries within one working day on all but three occasions during the year. Site visits were made at the requested frequency (quarterly) and the annual account review took place on 12 December 2024 at the supplier's regional office.

**Report Ref:** PER/2024/S03-015
**Period Covered:** 01 January 2024 – 31 December 2024
**Date of Issue:** 17 January 2025
**Prepared By:** Procurement Contracts Team, South East Region
**Distribution:** Finance Director; Commercial Manager; Regional Procurement Manager; Hanson Building Materials Ltd (Supplier Contact)

---

**1. INTRODUCTION**

This report presents the annual performance evaluation of Hanson Building Materials Ltd (supplier code HBM-015) for the calendar year 2024. The assessment is based on delivery records, quality inspection reports, site feedback, and commercial correspondence held by the Procurement Department. The purpose of the review is to determine the supplier's continued suitability for the approved vendor list and to identify areas for improvement ahead of the 2025 framework agreement.

The rating scale used throughout this report is 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). A score of 3.0 is considered the minimum acceptable threshold for continued inclusion on the approved supplier list without a corrective action plan. Scores below this threshold trigger a formal performance review meeting.

**2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

Hanson Building Materials Ltd has maintained a strong performance record throughout the 2024 evaluation period. The supplier has consistently met the project delivery schedules for the Northgate Retail Park development and the A12 Junction Improvement Scheme, with only two minor delays recorded, both of which were resolved within 48 hours and did not impact the critical path.

The overall supplier rating for the 2024 review period is **4.2 out of 5.0**, reflecting a solid performance across all assessed categories. This rating is current as of the date of issue of this report and supersedes the interim mid-year score of 3.9 issued in July 2024. The supplier evaluation report for Hanson Building Materials Ltd rates has_supplier_rating 4.2. Record status: current.

Areas of particular strength include material quality consistency, responsiveness to site queries, and adherence to health and safety documentation requirements. The primary area for improvement identified during the period is delivery punctuality on smaller, ad-hoc orders, where performance was marginally below the target level.

**3. SCORING METHODOLOGY**

Each performance category is scored based on a weighted average of monthly assessments submitted by site managers and the procurement team. Monthly assessment forms are completed within five working days of the end of each month, with a consolidated score calculated by the Procurement Contracts Team. The categories and their respective weightings for 2024 are as follows:

| Category | Weighting |
|----------|-----------|
| Delivery Punctuality | 30% |
| Quality of Materials | 35% |
| Commercial Responsiveness | 15% |
| Health & Safety Documentation | 10% |
| Communication & After-Sales Support | 10% |

Individual monthly scores are recorded in the supplier performance database (reference SP-2024-HBM). A summary of the quarterly scores is provided in Section 5 below.

**4. DELIVERY PUNCTUALITY**

Delivery punctuality is assessed against the agreed delivery dates and times specified on purchase orders. For the 2024 period, a total of 214 deliveries were scheduled across all active projects. Of these, 198 were delivered on time or early, representing a punctuality rate of 92.5%. This is slightly below the internal target of 95% but remains within the acceptable range for the rating scale.

The table below presents the consolidated monthly scores by quarter for the 2024 review period. Scores are the weighted average per the methodology in Section 3. All scores are recorded in the supplier performance database (reference SP-2024-HBM).

| **Annual** | **4.0** | **4.5** | **4.1** | **4.6** | **4.2** | **4.2** |

The Q3 dip in delivery punctuality corresponds to the period when ad-hoc order lead times were extended due to the supplier's internal transport reorganisation. This was raised at the quarterly review meeting on 3 October 2024 and a corrective action plan was agreed. Improvement was observed in Q4.

**6. PERFORMANCE BY CATEGORY – DETAILED COMMENTS**

**6.1 Delivery Punctuality (Annual score: 4.0)**

As noted in Section 4, the annual punctuality rate was 92.5%. The shortfall against the 95% target was concentrated in small orders under £500 and in deliveries to the North Shields site, where access restrictions occasionally required re-timing. The supplier's transport team has proposed a revised delivery window for that site, effective from February 2025.

**6.2 Quality of Materials (Annual score: 4.5)**

Material quality was consistently high throughout the year. No NCRs were raised against Hanson Building Materials Ltd in 2024. One minor issue was noted in June regarding a batch of bagged cement that had hardened due to storage conditions at the supplier's depot; this was replaced within 48 hours at no cost. The site team at the Riverside development reported no repeat occurrences.

**6.3 Commercial Responsiveness (Annual score: 4.1)**

Quotations for variations and new orders were returned within the agreed 5-working-day period in 89% of cases. The remaining 11% were delayed by an average of 2 working days, usually where pricing required confirmation from the supplier's regional office. Pricing remained competitive against the benchmark rates held by the procurement team.

**6.4 Health & Safety Documentation (Annual score: 4.6)**

All safety data sheets, delivery notes, and vehicle documentation were received in good order. The supplier's drivers have consistently complied with site induction requirements. No instances of missing or incomplete documentation were recorded during the period.

**6.5 Communication & After-Sales Support (Annual score: 4.2)**

The named account manager responded to email queries within one working day on all but three occasions during the year. Site visits were made at the requested frequency (quarterly) and the annual account review took place on 12 December 2024 at the supplier's regional office.
